title: AI vendors are switching from subscriptions to consumption pricing. AI PCs are the hedge.

content_html:
TL;DR

AI vendors are shifting from per-seat subscriptions to token consumption pricing. AI PCs running local models give enterprises cost predictability as cloud AI bills climb.

The AI pricing model is shifting. Major software vendors are moving away from per-seat subscriptions toward token consumption or outcome-based pricing for AI features. The flat-rate subscriptions that attracted early adopters were loss leaders. Now that enterprises are dependent on the tools, vendors need them to generate revenue. “We believe software value should align directly with customer success, not headcount,” said Zendesk’s president for products, engineering and AI, Shashi Upadhyay. For enterprises, that means AI is about to become significantly more expensive, and less predictable.

The hedge is local compute. AI PCs with neural processing units can now run small models locally, handling basic and mid-level generative tasks without sending a token to the cloud. Consumers and knowledge workers have been buying Mac Minis to run OpenClaw’s AI agent locally, avoiding per-query costs entirely. For enterprises running thousands of routine AI tasks daily, summarisation, drafting, code completion, and data extraction, a one-time hardware investment with zero marginal cost per query is increasingly attractive compared to a cloud bill that scales with usage.

The economics are straightforward. Cloud AI charges per token processed. Local AI charges nothing per query after the hardware purchase. The DRAM crisis has pushed memory costs higher, making AI PCs more expensive to buy, but the cost-per-query advantage still holds for high-volume, low-complexity tasks. The break-even point depends on how many queries a worker runs per day and how much the cloud vendor charges per token. For heavy users, the payback period on a $1,500 AI PC is months, not years.

Cloud computing is not going away. Training frontier models, running complex multi-step agents, and processing enterprise-scale data still require cloud infrastructure. The shift is not cloud versus local. It is which tasks belong where. Alphabet raised its capex guidance to $205 billion this year as Google Cloud revenue jumped 82%, and the hyperscalers are building for a world where cloud AI demand keeps growing. But the pricing shift from subscriptions to consumption gives enterprises a reason to move every task that can run locally off the cloud, keeping the expensive infrastructure for the tasks that genuinely need it. The AI PC is not a replacement for the cloud. It is a circuit breaker on the bill.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

人工智能供应商正在从按席位订阅转向代币消费定价。 随着云人工智能费用的攀升，运行本地模型的人工智能电脑为企业提供了成本可预测性。

人工智能的定价模式正在发生变化。 主要软件供应商正在从按席位订阅转向代币消费或基于结果的人工智能功能定价。 吸引早期采用者的统一费率订阅是亏损领先者。 既然企业依赖这些工具，供应商就需要它们来创收。 Zendesk 产品、工程和人工智能总裁 Shashi Upadhyay 表示：“我们认为软件价值应该与客户的成功直接挂钩，而不是与员工数量挂钩。” 对于企业来说，这意味着人工智能将变得更加昂贵，并且更难以预测。

对冲是本地计算。 具有神经处理单元的人工智能电脑现在可以在本地运行小型模型，处理基本和中级生成任务，而无需将令牌发送到云端。 消费者和知识工作者一直在购买 Mac Mini 来在本地运行 OpenClaw 的 AI 代理，从而完全避免每次查询的成本。 对于每天运行数千个常规人工智能任务、总结、起草、代码完成和数据提取的企业来说，与随使用量扩展的云账单相比，每次查询边际成本为零的一次性硬件投资越来越有吸引力。

经济学很简单。 Cloud AI 按处理的令牌收费。 购买硬件后，本地人工智能每次查询不收取任何费用。 DRAM 危机推高了内存成本，使得 AI PC 的购买成本更高，但对于大批量、低复杂性的任务来说，每次查询成本的优势仍然存在。 盈亏平衡点取决于工作人员每天运行的查询数量以及云供应商对每个令牌收取的费用。 对于重度用户来说，一台 1,500 美元的人工智能 PC 的投资回收期是几个月，而不是几年。

云计算不会消失。 训练前沿模型、运行复杂的多步骤代理以及处理企业规模的数据仍然需要云基础设施。 这种转变不是云与本地的转变。 这是哪些任务属于哪里。 随着谷歌云收入增长 82%，Alphabet 今年将资本支出指引提高至 2050 亿美元，而超大规模企业正在为云 AI 需求持续增长的世界而建设。 但从订阅到消费的定价转变让企业有理由将每项可以在本地运行的任务移出云，为真正需要的任务保留昂贵的基础设施。 AI PC 并不能替代云。 这是账单上的断路器。
